title: Foreign Issuers Flock To Euro Debt
text:
Foreign Issuers Flock To Euro Debt

August Gudmundsson

Gavekal Research | 3 Aug 2026

Non-residents are issuing more euro-denominated debt into the eurozone than ever before. In the first six months of 2026, non-residents issued a record €352bn, up from €287bn in the same period of 2025 and more than triple the first-half average for 2021-24 of €108bn. Yet despite the weight of issuance, markets have absorbed the additional flow easily as European institutional investors have queued up to buy high-quality euro assets. Rather than crowding out domestic borrowers, the boom in non-resident issuance appears to be deepening the euro credit market, attracting additional capital and making it easier for domestic companies to continue their gradual shift towards capital markets financing.
